messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator with pack purchases/opening, collection progression, unlocks, rebirth, and duplicate handling.

## Requirements
- Buy and open card packs; collect cards.
- Add leveling and progression unlocks: collection journal at level 2, pack storage at level 5, multiple-pack purchases at level 9, card hunting at level 12, and improved card odds on rebirth.
- Card tiers requested: “normal,gold,normal,diamond,godlike,special,secret.” The implementation interpreted the repeated “normal” as an additional Rare tier.
- For duplicates, allow selling or sending them to trash.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone responsive browser game with localStorage saves and three original themed pack types.
- Packs contain three cards; rebirth unlocks at level 15, preserves collection, and resets level, coins, and stored packs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the playable game UI and gameplay logic in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added level progression, feature locks/unlocks, pack buying/opening, storage, journal, hunting, rebirth, and duplicate sell/trash/keep actions.
- `node --check game.js` passed; game opened successfully in browser at `http://localhost:3002`.

### Active
- Browser check reported one console error, likely the missing favicon: `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found) @ http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico:0`.
- Visual screenshot check was not completed.

### Blocked
- No known blockers.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the UI with a screenshot at `http://localhost:3002` and verify layout/gameplay interactions.
2. Consider adding a favicon or suppressing the 404, then recheck console.
3. Review git status; changes are uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and views.
- `styles.css`: Responsive visual design and card/pack styling.
- `game.js`: Card catalog, game state, unlocks, saves, and interactions.

## Important Context
- Browser runtime opened successfully; initial console error was only a request for `/favicon.ico`.
- `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` was run and completed.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator with collection, progression, unlocks, rebirth, and duplicate handling.

## Requirements
- Buy and open card packs; collect cards.
- Unlock the collection journal at level 2, pack storage at level 5, multiple-pack purchases at level 9, and card hunting at level 12.
- Improve card odds with rebirth.
- Include the requested card tiers: “normal,gold,normal,diamond,godlike,special,secret.”
- Let players sell or trash duplicate cards.

## Decisions
- Implemented a standalone responsive browser game with localStorage saves and three original themed packs.
- Interpreted the repeated “normal” tier as an additional Rare tier.
- Packs contain three cards; rebirth unlocks at level 15, preserves the collection, and resets level, coins, and stored packs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game UI and mechanics for pack purchases/opening, collection, progression, unlocks, storage, journal, hunting, rebirth, and duplicate handling.
- Added a favicon and fixed the malformed title tag.
- Verified `node --check game.js`, opened the game in browser, checked the home screenshot, opened a pack and confirmed three results, and rechecked the console with zero errors.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Review git status and continue from the current uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and views.
- `styles.css`: Responsive visual design and card/pack styling.
- `game.js`: Card catalog, game state, unlocks, saves, and interactions.
- `favicon.svg`: Custom game favicon.
- `screenshots/home.jpg`: Home-page visual check.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser check at `http://localhost:3002` showed no console errors after the favicon fix.

# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Turn the existing Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D-style room game: use the phone to open Ordermart, order packs, unbox desk deliveries, and decide each card’s fate.
- Add more card packs while preserving the existing collection and progression game.

## Requirements
- Show a room with a desk, shelves, and other objects; let the player tap a phone button to pick it up and open Ordermart.
- Ordered packs should appear on the desk. Clicking a delivery starts an unboxing animation and card-by-card review.
- For each card, offer collection, sell, or trash actions.
- Add more card packs.

## Decisions
- Implement the room as a CSS-styled 3D-like scene rather than a Three.js scene.
- Purchases now create desk deliveries; card-by-card review occurs after unboxing.
- Added Frostbound Friends, Storm Chasers, and Wondergarden alongside the original three packs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added room, phone, Ordermart overlay, delivery, and unboxing/review markup in `index.html`.
- Added 21 cards and three packs to `game.js`.
- Reworked pack purchasing to create deliveries and added card review actions for keep, sell, or trash.

### Active
- Finish integrating the room gameplay: room rendering, phone store UI, delivery interactions, and wire-up for the new review flow.
- Remove or reconcile legacy pack modal/storage behavior and verify all original game features still work.
- Add room, phone, delivery, and unboxing styles; test responsive behavior and browser interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement `renderRoom()`, `closePhone()`, `roomToast()`, and the Ordermart phone UI in `game.js`; add click handlers for phone, ordering, delivery unboxing, review actions, and returning to the room.
2. Update the storage delivery button handler and remove references to obsolete `openPacks()`/stored-pack workflow where appropriate.
3. Add responsive room/gameplay CSS in `styles.css`, then run syntax and browser checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Room scene, phone overlay, unboxing overlay, and existing game UI.
- `game.js`: Card catalog, pack catalog, purchase/delivery state, review flow, and legacy game interactions.
- `styles.css`: Existing responsive game styling; room and overlay styles still needed.
- `favicon.svg`: Existing custom favicon.

## Important Context
- Existing changes are uncommitted; project files were previously untracked.
- `game.js` now calls functions that have not yet been implemented: `renderRoom()`, `closePhone()`, and `roomToast()`.
- Existing shop controls still call `buyPack()`, but the intended new flow is phone-based ordering.
- The storage view now lists `state.deliveries`; the event handler still references obsolete `data-open-stored` and needs updating.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D-style room game where players order packs by phone, unbox desk deliveries, and decide each card’s fate.
- Add more card packs while preserving collection and progression features.

## Requirements
- Show a room with a desk, shelves, and other objects; let the player pick up a phone and open Ordermart.
- Ordered packs appear on the desk; clicking a delivery starts unboxing and card-by-card review.
- Let players add each card to their collection, sell it, or trash it.
- Add more card packs.

## Decisions
- Build the room as a CSS-styled 3D-like scene rather than using Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review happens after unboxing.
- Add Frostbound Friends, Storm Chasers, and Wondergarden alongside the original packs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added room, phone, Ordermart, delivery, and unboxing markup to `index.html`.
- Added 21 cards and three packs to `game.js`.
- Changed pack purchases to create deliveries and implemented card-by-card keep, sell, or trash review.
- Implemented room rendering, Ordermart UI, phone controls, delivery interactions, and storage delivery buttons.
- Added responsive CSS for the room, phone overlay, deliveries, unboxing, and mobile layouts.

### Active
- Reconcile legacy shop, stored-pack, and pack-modal UI with the new phone-order flow.
- Test syntax, ordering, delivery unboxing, card decisions, saving, progression, and responsive browser behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and reconcile the legacy `.app-shell`, `openPacks()`, duplicate-review, stored-pack, and modal workflows with the room-first flow.
2. Check for broken handlers or state paths, including whether the old shop and stored packs remain usable without duplicating purchase flows.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for ordering, unboxing, card decisions, saving, and collection/progression features.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Room and gameplay overlays, plus legacy shop and modal markup.
- `game.js`: Card and pack catalogs, state, ordering, delivery, review, and game interactions.
- `styles.css`: Existing app styles and newly added room/overlay/responsive styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `renderRoom()`, `renderOrdermart()`, `openPhone()`, `closePhone()`, and `roomToast()` are implemented; `render()` calls `renderRoom()`.
- The room scene and legacy `.app-shell` are both present in `index.html`; their intended visibility and relationship still need reconciliation.
- `buyPack()` creates desk deliveries; legacy shop buy buttons now open Ordermart.
- `startUnbox()` supports resuming `state.activeReview`; review choices use `data-review`.
- `renderStorage()` lists deliveries, but the old storage copy still refers to stored packs.

11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.

22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy room-first game where players order packs by phone, unbox desk deliveries, and decide each card’s fate.
- Add Frostbound Friends, Storm Chasers, and Wondergarden while preserving collection and progression features.

## Requirements
- Show a room with a desk and shelves, with a phone-based shop.
- Ordered packs appear as desk deliveries; review cards individually to keep, sell, or trash.
- Keep collection and progression features accessible alongside the room.

## Decisions
- Use a CSS-styled 3D-like scene rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop buttons open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added room, phone, Ordermart, desk-delivery, and unboxing markup and styling.
- Added 21 cards and three new packs; purchases create deliveries, and review supports keep, sell, or trash.
- Added room rendering, Ordermart UI, delivery interactions, and storage entries.
- Added room shortcuts for Collection and Workshop; corrected duplicate view-rendering statements in `setView()`.
- Updated storage copy to describe desk deliveries.
- `node --check game.js` passed earlier in the work.

### Active
- Reconcile obsolete `openPacks()`, `packModal`, `data-duplicate`, and undefined `resolveDuplicate` paths.
- Check room/workshop navigation and overlays, including whether stored delivery actions remain usable.
- Test ordering, unboxing, card decisions, saving, progression, and responsive layouts.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Remove or reconcile the legacy pack modal and duplicate-review code paths.
2. Check delivery behavior, navigation, and rebirth handling for stored deliveries.
3. Run browser checks for ordering, unboxing, card decisions, persistence, progression, and mobile layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Room, overlays, workshop, and legacy modal markup.
- `game.js`: Card and pack catalogs, state, ordering, delivery, review, and navigation.
- `styles.css`: Room, overlay, responsive, and legacy application styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in the current repository status.
- `buyPack()` creates desk deliveries; `startUnbox()` supports resuming `state.activeReview`; review buttons use `data-review`.
- `openPacks()` and the old pack modal remain; click delegation still references `data-duplicate` and `resolveDuplicate`, which has no definition.
- `rebirth()` resets `state.stored` but not `state.deliveries`; stored deliveries are represented by `state.deliveries`.
- `setView()` scrolls to `.app-shell`; room and legacy workshop markup coexist.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy room-first game where players order packs by phone, unbox desk deliveries, and decide each card’s fate.
- Add Frostbound Friends, Storm Chasers, and Wondergarden while preserving collection and progression features.

## Requirements
- Show a room with a desk and shelves, with a phone-based shop.
- Ordered packs appear as desk deliveries; review cards individually to keep, sell, or trash.
- Keep collection and progression features accessible alongside the room.

## Decisions
- Use a CSS-styled 3D-like scene rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop buttons open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added room, phone, Ordermart, desk-delivery, and unboxing markup and styling.
- Added 21 cards and three new packs; purchases create deliveries, and review supports keep, sell, or trash.
- Added room rendering, Ordermart UI, delivery interactions, and storage entries.
- Removed the obsolete pack-opening flow, duplicate-review handler, and legacy pack modal markup and listeners.
- Updated storage count to report packs rather than delivery bundles.
- Updated rebirth to clear unopened deliveries while preserving cards currently under review.

### Active
- Validate navigation, delivery unboxing and resuming, save/persistence, progression, rebirth, and responsive layouts.
- Check browser console and runtime behavior after the legacy path removals.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check game.js` and inspect for remaining legacy modal or duplicate-review references.
2. Test ordering, delivery unboxing, keep/sell/trash, interrupted review resume, and persistence.
3. Check workshop/collection navigation and mobile layouts; add a clear return path from the workshop to the room if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Room, overlays, workshop, and navigation markup.
- `game.js`: Card and pack catalogs, state, ordering, delivery, review, and navigation.
- `styles.css`: Room, overlay, responsive, and workshop styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in the current repository status.
- `startUnbox()` supports resuming `state.activeReview`; review buttons use `data-review`.
- A proposed room-return button markup edit failed because the target text was not found; no room-return control was added.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy room-first game where players order packs by phone, unbox desk deliveries, and decide each card’s fate.
- Add Frostbound Friends, Storm Chasers, and Wondergarden while preserving collection and progression features.

## Requirements
- Show a room with a desk and shelves, with a phone-based shop.
- Ordered packs appear as desk deliveries; review cards individually to keep, sell, or trash.
- Keep collection and progression features accessible alongside the room.

## Decisions
- Use a CSS-styled 3D-like scene rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop buttons open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added room, phone, Ordermart, desk-delivery, and unboxing markup and styling.
- Added 21 cards and three new packs; purchases create deliveries, and review supports keep, sell, or trash.
- Added room rendering, Ordermart UI, delivery interactions, and storage entries.
- Removed the obsolete pack-opening flow, duplicate-review handler, and legacy pack modal markup and listeners.
- Updated storage count to report packs rather than delivery bundles.
- Updated rebirth to clear unopened deliveries while preserving cards currently under review.
- Added the missing `roomReturn` button to the workshop header in `index.html`.
- `node --check game.js` passed; headless Chromium rendered the page and dynamically populated the pack grid.

### Active
- Validate ordering, delivery unboxing and resume, keep/sell/trash, persistence, progression, rebirth, navigation, and responsive layouts.
- Inspect browser console/runtime behavior and verify desktop/mobile layouts.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Exercise ordering, delivery unboxing/resume, review choices, persistence, progression, rebirth, and navigation in a browser.
2. Check desktop and mobile layouts and inspect for runtime errors.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Room, overlays, workshop, navigation, and the new `roomReturn` control.
- `game.js`: Card and pack catalogs, state, ordering, delivery, review, and navigation.
- `styles.css`: Room, overlay, responsive, workshop, and `roomReturn` styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in the current repository status.
- `startUnbox()` supports resuming `state.activeReview`; review buttons use `data-review`.
- Headless Chromium’s DOM output showed the page initialized and populated the pack grid; only SQLite shutdown warnings appeared in the captured output.

# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with a working Ordermart, distinctive card art, and a battle mode.

## Requirements
- “Pls make the room 3D also fix that pick up phone button doesnt work also make taht you can only enter shop menu by opening ordermart not scrolling down also add a special CGI sprite for every pokemon card also add battle mode at level 13”

## Decisions
- Use a CSS-styled 3D-like scene rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation should open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added room, phone, Ordermart, desk-delivery, unboxing, and workshop navigation.
- Added 21 cards and three new packs; purchases create deliveries, and review supports keep, sell, or trash.
- Added Battle arena navigation and view markup gated at level 13.
- Added seeded CGI-style card-art markup for collection cards.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Wire `[data-open-phone]` clicks and fix phone click handling to use `closest('#phoneButton')`.
- Ensure shop access is only through Ordermart; shop view markup remains in `index.html`, though `setView('packs')` routes to the phone.
- Implement `renderBattle()` and battle selection/results interactions.
- Finish CGI-style artwork across journal, hunting, and unboxing displays; add art and battle CSS.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated `[data-open-phone]` click handling and use a `closest('#phoneButton')` check so nested phone elements work.
2. Implement battle rendering and selection/results; verify the level-13 lock.
3. Replace remaining emoji-only card displays with `creatureArt()` and add responsive CGI/battle styles.
4. Remove or reroute remaining shop-view access and confirm scrolling cannot expose the shop.
5. Run browser checks for phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, hidden pack-shop view, and battle view markup.
- `game.js`: Card catalog/rendering, navigation, phone handling, ordering, progression, and incomplete battle/art integration.
- `styles.css`: Room rendering and existing card visuals; CGI and battle styling remains to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `M game.js` and `M index.html`; `styles.css` is unchanged.
- Click delegation currently handles `[data-view]`, but not `[data-open-phone]`; phone handling only checks `event.target.id === 'phoneButton'`.
- `setView('packs')` calls `openPhone()`, but the legacy shop markup still exists in `index.html`.
- `renderBattle()` is referenced by `setView()` and `render()` but is not implemented.
- CGI markup currently appears only in collection cards; journal unknowns, hunting options, and unboxing remain emoji-based.

## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with a working Ordermart, distinctive card art, and a battle mode.

## Requirements
- “Pls make the room 3D also fix that pick up phone button doesnt work also make taht you can only enter shop menu by opening ordermart not scrolling down also add a special CGI sprite for every pokemon card also add battle mode at level 13”

## Decisions
- Use a CSS-styled 3D-like scene rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation should open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added room, phone, Ordermart, desk-delivery, unboxing, and workshop navigation.
- Added 21+ cards and multiple packs; purchases create deliveries, and review supports keep, sell, or trash.
- Added Battle arena markup and navigation gated at level 13.
- Added seeded CGI-style card-art markup for collection cards.
- `node --check game.js` passed previously.

### Active
- Wire `[data-open-phone]` clicks and fix phone click handling to use `closest('#phoneButton')`.
- Implement `renderBattle()` and battle selection/results interactions.
- Finish CGI-style artwork across journal, hunting, and unboxing displays; add art and battle CSS.
- Remove or reroute remaining shop-view access and confirm scrolling cannot expose the shop.
- Run browser checks for phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated `[data-open-phone]` click handling and use a `closest('#phoneButton')` check so nested phone elements work.
2. Implement battle rendering and selection/results; verify the level-13 lock.
3. Replace remaining emoji-only card displays with `creatureArt()` and add responsive CGI/battle styles.
4. Remove or reroute remaining shop-view access and confirm scrolling cannot expose the shop.
5. Run browser checks for phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, hidden pack-shop view, and battle view markup.
- `game.js`: Card catalog/rendering, navigation, phone handling, ordering, progression, and incomplete battle/art integration.
- `styles.css`: Room rendering and existing card visuals; CGI and battle styling remains to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; latest known status showed modified `game.js` and `index.html`, with `styles.css` unchanged.
- Click delegation handles `[data-view]` but not `[data-open-phone]`; phone handling only checks `event.target.id === 'phoneButton'`.
- `setView('packs')` calls `openPhone()`, but legacy shop markup remains in `index.html`.
- `renderBattle()` is referenced by `setView()` and `render()` but is not implemented.
- CGI markup currently appears only in collection cards; journal unknowns, hunting options, and unboxing remain emoji-based.

- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation should open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added the room scene, desk deliveries, unboxing, phone overlay, Ordermart navigation, and level-9 multi-pack orders.
- Added 21+ cards and multiple packs, with keep, sell, or trash review actions.
- Added battle arena markup and level-13 navigation gating.
- Added seeded CGI-style card-art markup for collection cards.

### Active

- Implement `renderBattle()` and battle selection/results interactions; it is referenced by `render()` and `setView()` but is not defined.
- Extend CGI-style art to journal, hunting, and unboxing displays; those currently use emoji-only card displays.
- Add battle and CGI artwork styling.
- Confirm shop access is only through Ordermart, including ensuring scrolling cannot expose the legacy `view-packs`.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Add delegated `[data-open-phone]` handling and use `closest('#phoneButton')` for phone clicks.
2. Implement battle rendering and selection/results, preserving the level-13 lock.
3. Replace emoji-only displays in journal, hunting, and unboxing with `creatureArt()` and add responsive art/battle styles.
4. Verify the legacy shop view cannot be reached by scrolling and that shop navigation opens Ordermart.
5. Run browser checks for phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, legacy shop view, and battle markup.
- `game.js`: Card catalog/rendering, phone handling, navigation, ordering, progression, and incomplete battle integration.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with a working Ordermart, distinctive card art, and a battle mode.

## Requirements
- “Pls make the room 3D also fix that pick up phone button doesnt work also make taht you can only enter shop menu by opening ordermart not scrolling down also add a special CGI sprite for every pokemon card also add battle mode at level 13”

## Decisions
- Use layered CSS 3D styling rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation should open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added room scene, desk deliveries, unboxing, phone overlay, Ordermart navigation, and level-9 multi-pack orders.
- Added 21+ cards and multiple packs, with keep, sell, or trash review actions.
- Added battle arena markup and level-13 navigation gating.
- Added seeded CGI-style card-art markup for collection cards.
- Added layered CSS 3D room styling.
- Updated undiscovered journal cards to use `creatureArt()`.

### Active
- Fix phone activation: delegated click handling does not handle `[data-open-phone]`; phone handler only checks `event.target.id === 'phoneButton'`.
- Implement `renderBattle()` and battle selection/results interactions; it is referenced by `render()` and `setView()` but undefined.
- Extend CGI-style art to hunting and unboxing displays; currently emoji-only.
- Add battle and CGI artwork styling.
- Ensure shop access is only through Ordermart, including preventing scrolling to the legacy `view-packs`.
- Verify phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated `[data-open-phone]` handling and use `closest('#phoneButton')` for phone clicks.
2. Implement battle rendering and selection/results while preserving the level-13 lock.
3. Replace emoji-only displays in hunting and unboxing with `creatureArt()` and add responsive art/battle styles.
4. Ensure the legacy shop view cannot be reached by scrolling and that shop navigation opens Ordermart.
5. Run browser checks for phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, legacy shop view, and battle markup.
- `game.js`: Card catalog/rendering, phone handling, navigation, ordering, progression, and incomplete battle integration.
- `styles.css`: Room and existing card styling; CGI and battle styling remains to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `game.js` and `index.html` are modified, and `styles.css` was unchanged in the latest status check.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest journal rendering edit.
- `renderBattle()` is referenced but missing.
- Shop markup remains in `index.html`; `setView('packs')` opens the phone, and the storage shop button routes there.

## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with a working Ordermart, distinctive card art, and a battle mode.

## Requirements
- “Pls make the room 3D also fix that pick up phone button doesnt work also make taht you can only enter shop menu by opening ordermart not scrolling down also add a special CGI sprite for every pokemon card also add battle mode at level 13”

## Decisions
- Use layered CSS 3D styling rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation should open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added room scene, desk deliveries, unboxing, phone overlay, Ordermart navigation, and level-9 multi-pack orders.
- Added 21+ cards and multiple packs, with keep, sell, or trash review actions.
- Added battle arena markup and level-13 navigation gating.
- Added seeded CGI-style card-art markup for collection and journal cards.
- Added layered CSS 3D room styling.
- Added `renderBattle()`, battle card markup, and randomized opponent/results logic with coin and XP rewards.

### Active
- Fix phone activation: delegated click handling does not handle `[data-open-phone]`; phone handler only checks `event.target.id === 'phoneButton'`.
- Add battle selection/start click handling; current renderer and `runBattle()` lack delegated event listeners.
- Extend CGI-style art to hunting and unboxing displays; currently emoji-only.
- Add battle and CGI artwork styling.
- Ensure shop access is only through Ordermart, including preventing scrolling to the legacy `view-packs`.
- Verify phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated `[data-open-phone]` handling and handle clicks inside the phone with `closest('#phoneButton')`.
2. Wire `[data-battle-card]` selection and `#battleStart` to `renderBattle()` and `runBattle()`.
3. Replace emoji-only displays in hunting and unboxing with `creatureArt()` and add responsive art/battle styles.
4. Ensure the legacy shop view cannot be reached by scrolling and that shop navigation opens Ordermart.
5. Run browser checks for phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, legacy shop view, and battle markup.
- `game.js`: Card catalog/rendering, phone handling, navigation, ordering, progression, and battle implementation.
- `styles.css`: Room styling; CGI and battle styling remains to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `game.js` and `index.html` are modified, and `styles.css` has existing room styling.
- `renderBattle()` is now defined and called by `render()` and `setView()`, but battle interaction handlers are still missing.
- Shop markup remains in `index.html`; `setView('packs')` opens the phone, and the storage shop button routes there.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with a working Ordermart, distinctive card art, and a battle mode.

## Requirements
- “Pls make the room 3D also fix that pick up phone button doesnt work also make taht you can only enter shop menu by opening ordermart not scrolling down also add a special CGI sprite for every pokemon card also add battle mode at level 13”

## Decisions
- Use layered CSS 3D styling rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation should open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added room scene, desk deliveries, Ordermart navigation, multi-pack ordering, seeded CGI-style card art for collection and journal, and battle arena/rendering with randomized outcomes and coin/XP rewards.
- Added layered CSS 3D room styling.
- `node --check game.js` passes.

### Active
- Fix phone activation: delegated click handling does not handle `[data-open-phone]`; phone handler only checks `event.target.id === 'phoneButton'`.
- Add battle selection/start click handling; renderer and `runBattle()` lack delegated event listeners.
- Extend CGI-style art to hunting and unboxing displays; currently emoji-only.
- Add battle and CGI artwork styling.
- Ensure the legacy shop view cannot be reached by scrolling and shop navigation opens Ordermart.
- Verify phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated `[data-open-phone]` handling and handle clicks inside the phone with `closest('#phoneButton')`.
2. Wire `[data-battle-card]` selection and `#battleStart` to `renderBattle()` and `runBattle()`.
3. Replace emoji-only displays in hunting and unboxing with `creatureArt()` and add responsive art/battle styles.
4. Ensure the legacy shop view cannot be reached by scrolling and shop navigation opens Ordermart.
5. Run browser checks for phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Card catalog/rendering, phone handling, navigation, ordering, progression, and battle implementation.
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, legacy shop view, and battle markup.
- `styles.css`: Room styling; CGI and battle styling remains to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `game.js` and `index.html` are modified. `styles.css` has existing room styling.
- `renderBattle()` is called by `render()` and `setView()`, but battle interaction handlers are still missing.
- Shop markup remains in `index.html`; `setView('packs')` opens the phone, and the storage shop button routes there.

## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with a working Ordermart, distinctive card art, and a battle mode.

## Requirements
- “Pls make the room 3D also fix that pick up phone button doesnt work also make taht you can only enter shop menu by opening ordermart not scrolling down also add a special CGI sprite for every pokemon card also add battle mode at level 13”

## Decisions
- Use layered CSS 3D styling rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation should open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a room scene, desk deliveries, Ordermart navigation, multi-pack ordering, seeded CGI-style card art for collection and journal, and a battle arena/rendering with randomized outcomes and coin/XP rewards.
- Added layered CSS 3D room styling.
- `node --check game.js` passes.

### Active
- Fix phone activation: delegated click handling does not handle `[data-open-phone]`; the phone handler only checks `event.target.id === 'phoneButton'`.
- Wire battle selection and start click handling; `renderBattle()` and `runBattle()` lack delegated event listeners.
- Extend CGI-style art to hunting and unboxing displays; currently emoji-only.
- Add battle and CGI artwork styling.
- Ensure the legacy shop view cannot be reached by scrolling and shop navigation opens Ordermart.
- Verify phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated `[data-open-phone]` handling and handle clicks inside the phone with `closest('#phoneButton')`.
2. Wire `[data-battle-card]` selection and `#battleStart` to `renderBattle()` and `runBattle()`.
3. Replace emoji-only displays in hunting and unboxing with `creatureArt()` and add responsive art/battle styles.
4. Ensure the legacy shop view cannot be reached by scrolling and shop navigation opens Ordermart.
5. Run browser checks for phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Card catalog/rendering, phone handling, navigation, ordering, progression, and battle implementation.
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, legacy shop view, and battle markup.
- `styles.css`: Room styling; CGI and battle styling remains to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `game.js` and `index.html` are modified. `styles.css` has existing room styling.
- `renderBattle()` is called by `render()` and `setView()`, but battle interaction handlers are still missing.
- Shop markup remains in `index.html`; `setView('packs')` opens the phone, and the storage shop button routes there.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with a working Ordermart, distinctive card art, and a battle mode.

## Requirements
- “Pls make the room 3D also fix that pick up phone button doesnt work also make taht you can only enter shop menu by opening ordermart not scrolling down also add a special CGI sprite for every pokemon card also add battle mode at level 13”

## Decisions
- Use layered CSS 3D styling rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation should open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a room scene with layered CSS 3D styling, desk deliveries, Ordermart navigation, multi-pack ordering, seeded CGI-style card art in the collection and journal, and a level-13 battle arena implementation.
- `node --check game.js` passes.

### Active
- Fix phone activation: delegated click handling does not handle `[data-open-phone]`; current phone handler only checks `event.target.id === 'phoneButton'`.
- Wire battle selection and start click handling; `renderBattle()` and `runBattle()` exist, but have no delegated event listeners.
- Extend CGI-style art to hunting and unboxing; hunting and unboxing remain emoji-only.
- Add battle and CGI artwork styling; `styles.css` currently has room styling but no corresponding CGI/battle styles.
- Ensure the legacy shop view cannot be reached by scrolling and shop navigation opens Ordermart.
- Verify phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated `[data-open-phone]` handling and handle clicks inside the phone with `closest('#phoneButton')`.
2. Wire `[data-battle-card]` selection and `#battleStart` to `renderBattle()` and `runBattle()`.
3. Replace emoji-only displays in hunting and unboxing with `creatureArt()` and add responsive artwork/battle styles.
4. Ensure the legacy shop view cannot be reached by scrolling and shop navigation opens Ordermart.
5. Run browser checks for phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Card catalog/rendering, phone handling, navigation, ordering, progression, and battle implementation.
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, legacy shop view, and battle markup.
- `styles.css`: Room styling; CGI and battle styling remains to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `game.js` and `index.html` are modified. `styles.css` has existing room styling.
- The `view-packs` shop markup remains in `index.html`; `setView('packs')` opens the phone, and the storage shop button routes there.
- Battle unlock is configured at level 13.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with a working Ordermart, distinctive card art, and a battle mode.

## Requirements
- “Pls make the room 3D also fix that pick up phone button doesnt work also make taht you can only enter shop menu by opening ordermart not scrolling down also add a special CGI sprite for every pokemon card also add battle mode at level 13”

## Decisions
- Use layered CSS 3D styling rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation should open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added layered CSS 3D room styling, desk deliveries, Ordermart navigation, multi-pack ordering, seeded CGI-style card art in the collection and journal, and a level-13 battle arena implementation.
- `node --check game.js` passed in earlier work.

### Active
- Fix phone activation: delegated clicks do not handle `[data-open-phone]`; checking only `event.target.id === 'phoneButton'` also misses clicks on phone descendants.
- Wire `[data-battle-card]` selection and `#battleStart` to `renderBattle()` and `runBattle()`; implementations exist but delegated event listeners do not.
- Extend CGI-style art to hunting and unboxing, which still display emoji-only art; add responsive CGI and battle styling.
- Verify the legacy shop cannot be reached by scrolling and shop navigation opens Ordermart.
- Browser-check phone/Ordermart, battles, artwork, and desktop/mobile layout.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated `[data-open-phone]` handling and use `closest('#phoneButton')` for phone clicks.
2. Add delegated battle-card selection and battle-start handlers.
3. Use `creatureArt()` in hunting and unboxing; add CGI and battle styles.
4. Check shop navigation and legacy shop visibility/scroll access.
5. Run browser checks across phone, Ordermart, battles, artwork, and responsive layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Card art, phone/order handling, navigation, hunting, unboxing, and battle logic.
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, legacy shop view, and battle markup.
- `styles.css`: Room styling; CGI and battle styling remains to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `game.js` and `index.html` are modified. `styles.css` has existing room styling.
- The `view-packs` section remains in `index.html`; `setView('packs')` opens the phone, and storage’s shop button routes there.
- Battle unlock is configured at level 13.

## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with a working Ordermart, distinctive card art, and a battle mode.

## Requirements
- “Pls make the room 3D also fix that pick up phone button doesnt work also make taht you can only enter shop menu by opening ordermart not scrolling down also add a special CGI sprite for every pokemon card also add battle mode at level 13”

## Decisions
- Use layered CSS 3D styling rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation should open Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added layered CSS 3D room styling, desk deliveries, Ordermart navigation, multi-pack ordering, seeded CGI-style card art in the collection and journal, and a level-13 battle arena implementation.
- Fixed delegated handling for `[data-open-phone]` and phone button descendants.
- Added delegated battle-card selection and battle-start handlers.
- Extended CGI card art to hunting options and unboxing review.

### Active
- Add responsive CGI artwork and battle styles in `styles.css`.
- Verify the legacy shop cannot be reached by scrolling and that shop navigation opens Ordermart.
- Browser-check phone activation, Ordermart ordering, battle selection/results, card art, and desktop/mobile layouts.
- Run syntax checks and inspect the final diff.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Add responsive CGI artwork and battle styles in `styles.css`.
2. Verify Ordermart-only shop navigation and phone activation.
3. Browser-check battles, card art, and desktop/mobile layouts.
4. Run syntax checks and inspect the final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Card art, phone/order handling, navigation, hunting, unboxing, and battle logic.
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, hidden shop view, and battle markup.
- `styles.css`: Room styling exists; CGI artwork and battle styling remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `game.js` and `index.html` are modified. `styles.css` was not listed as modified in the latest `git status`.
- The shop section remains in `index.html` as `#view-packs` with `hidden`; `setView('packs')` opens the phone.
- Battle unlock is configured at level 13.
- The latest edits have not yet been validated.

## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with a working Ordermart, distinctive card art, and a battle mode.

## Requirements
- Make the room 3D, fix the nonworking pick-up-phone button, and allow shop access only through Ordermart rather than scrolling to the shop.
- Add special CGI-style sprite art for every Pokémon card and battle mode at level 13.

## Decisions
- Use layered CSS 3D styling rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries; card review follows unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation opens Ordermart; multi-pack ordering unlocks at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added layered CSS 3D room styling, desk deliveries, Ordermart navigation and ordering, seeded CGI-style card art, and level-13 battle implementation.
- Fixed delegated handling for `[data-open-phone]` and phone button descendants.
- Added delegated battle-card selection and battle-start handlers.
- Extended CGI card art to hunting options and unboxing review.
- Added responsive CGI art and battle styles to `styles.css`.
- `git diff --check` and `node --check game.js` passed before the latest browser-test attempt.

### Active
- Validate Ordermart ordering, unboxing, battle selection/results, card art, and desktop/mobile layouts.
- Inspect the final diff.

### Blocked
- Browser smoke test did not start: the local ChromeDriver request timed out while creating a session; browser behavior remains unverified.

## Next Move
1. Retry browser validation using an available browser setup; check phone activation, ordering/delivery, card review, level-13 battle, and responsive layout.
2. Run syntax checks and `git diff --check`, then inspect the final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Card art, phone/order handling, navigation, hunting, unboxing, and battle logic.
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, hidden shop view, and battle markup.
- `styles.css`: Room, CGI artwork, and battle styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css`.
- Battle unlock is configured at level 13.
- Browser smoke test attempted with `/usr/bin/chromedriver` and `/usr/bin/chromium`, but failed on a ChromeDriver request timeout.

## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with a working Ordermart, distinctive card art, and a battle mode.

## Requirements
- Make the room 3D, fix the pick-up-phone button, and make Ordermart the only way to access the shop.
- Add CGI-style art for every Pokémon card and unlock friendly card battles at level 13.

## Decisions
- Use layered CSS 3D styling rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries, followed by card review during unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation opens Ordermart; multi-pack orders unlock at level 9.
- Battle is a friendly duel using cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added layered CSS room styling, desk deliveries, Ordermart navigation and ordering, seeded CGI-style card art, and level-13 battle implementation.
- Fixed delegated handling for `[data-open-phone]` and phone button descendants.
- Added delegated battle-card selection and battle-start handlers.
- Extended CGI card art to hunting options and unboxing review; added responsive art and battle styles.
- `git diff --check` and `node --check game.js` passed before the latest browser-test attempt.

### Active
- Validate Ordermart ordering, unboxing, battle selection/results, card art, and desktop/mobile layouts.
- Inspect the final diff.

### Blocked
- Browser smoke test remains unverified: ChromeDriver session creation timed out in an earlier attempt, and the latest retry failed while reading the HTTP response.

## Next Move
1. Retry browser validation with an available browser setup; check phone activation, ordering/delivery, card review, level-13 battle, and responsive layout.
2. Run syntax checks and `git diff --check`, then inspect the final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Card art, phone/order handling, navigation, hunting, unboxing, and battle logic.
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, hidden shop view, and battle markup.
- `styles.css`: Room, CGI artwork, and battle styling.

## Important Context
- Changes in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css` are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with Ordermart ordering, distinctive card art, and friendly battles.

## Requirements
- Make the room 3D-style, fix the pick-up-phone button, and make Ordermart the only way to access the shop.
- Add CGI-style art for every Pokémon card and unlock friendly card battles at level 13.

## Decisions
- Use layered CSS 3D styling rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries, followed by card review during unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation opens Ordermart; multi-pack orders unlock at level 9.
- Battles use cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added CSS room styling, Ordermart navigation and ordering, desk deliveries, card art, and level-13 battle functionality.
- Fixed delegated handling for phone triggers, including button descendants; added battle selection and start handlers.
- `git diff --check` and `node --check game.js` passed; headless Chromium rendered `index.html` with `--dump-dom`.

### Active
- Validate ordering and delivery, unboxing card review, battle selection/results, and desktop/mobile layouts.
- Inspect the final diff.

### Blocked
- Interactive browser validation has not been completed: ChromeDriver session creation timed out and a retry failed reading the HTTP response. Selenium and Playwright Node packages are unavailable, but `playwright-cli` is present.

## Next Move
1. Try interactive validation using the available `playwright-cli` for phone activation, ordering/delivery, card review, battle, and responsive layouts.
2. Re-run syntax checks and `git diff --check`; inspect the final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Card art, phone/order handling, navigation, unboxing, and battle logic.
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, and battle markup.
- `styles.css`: Room, CGI-style card art, and battle styling.

## Important Context
- Changes in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css` are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Turn the Pokémon-inspired card pack simulator into a cozy 3D room-first game with Ordermart ordering, distinctive card art, and friendly battles.

## Requirements
- Make the room 3D-style, fix the pick-up-phone button, and make Ordermart the only way to access the shop.
- Add CGI-style art for every Pokémon card and unlock friendly card battles at level 13.

## Decisions
- Use layered CSS 3D styling rather than Three.js.
- Purchases create desk deliveries, followed by card review during unboxing.
- Workshop shop navigation opens Ordermart; multi-pack orders unlock at level 9.
- Battles use cards from the collection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added room styling, Ordermart navigation and ordering, desk deliveries, card art, and level-13 battles.
- Fixed delegated phone-trigger handling, including button descendants; added battle selection and start handlers.
- `git diff --check` and `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser opened via `playwright-cli`; verified room, phone overlay, Ordermart, and a pack order producing a desk delivery.

### Active
- Validate delivery unboxing/card review, battle selection and results, and desktop/mobile layouts.
- Inspect and finalize the diff.

### Blocked
- Browser validation is incomplete: clicking “Open card delivery” did not open the unboxing overlay; investigate whether delivery interaction works and continue testing.
- Unboxing’s first card review is delayed by 950 ms; that delay may matter when testing.

## Next Move
1. Investigate why clicking the desk delivery did not open unboxing; verify card review and keep/sell/trash flows.
2. Validate battle selection and results, including level-13 unlock, and test responsive layouts.
3. Re-run `git diff --check` and `node --check game.js`; inspect final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Card art, phone/order handling, navigation, unboxing, and battle logic.
- `index.html`: Room controls, phone overlay, navigation, and battle markup.
- `styles.css`: Room, CGI-style card, and battle styling.

## Important Context
- Changes in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css` are uncommitted.
- A local HTTP server was started on `http://127.0.0.1:8765`; Playwright Chromium was installed and the browser opened.
